submission.text: We did some work outside of this to migrate app-monitor from using app-issue-tracker to using swarm-manager. Not sure how complete/verified that migration is, but it likely affects the deprecation work completion status. Not sure where else app-issue-tracker is still used, as I think app-monitor was the primary place. Probably worth seeing how it was done there, verifying its accuracy and seeing what remaining work needs to be done (should ideally be a hard cutover with absolutely no compatability/legacy/dead code to the app-issue-tracker integration), and suggesting applying that same pattern to every other scenario that still integrates with app-issue-tracker

item.title: Verify and Finalize App-Monitor's Hard Cutover from App-Issue-Tracker to Swarm-Manager
item.description:
Verify the in-flight migration of app-monitor from app-issue-tracker to swarm-manager is a complete hard cutover with zero legacy/compat/dead code, then finalize it.

## Context

A migration is currently in progress (uncommitted changes touch `scenarios/app-monitor/api/services/app_reports.go`, `api/toolregistry/issue_tools.go`, `api/services/app_diagnostics_aggregator.go`, UI `ReportIssueDialog.tsx`, `useReportExistingIssues.ts`, `useReportIssueState.ts`, `scenarioIssuesStore.ts`, `DiagnosticsTab.tsx`, `LighthouseTab.tsx`, etc.). Completeness and correctness are unverified.

## Scope

1. Inventory every prior app-issue-tracker integration point in app-monitor (API client, tool handlers, UI dialog flows, types, tests, service.json, docs).
2. Confirm each one now routes to swarm-manager (capture / backlog / execution endpoints) with equivalent behavior, including the issue-report flow, the diagnostics → issue creation flow, and any agent-spawn flows.
3. Remove ALL residual references to app-issue-tracker — imports, types, env vars, service.json depends_on entries, fallback branches, dead helpers, comments, test fixtures, docs. No feature flags. No compat shims. No 'legacy mode'.
4. Update tests to assert against swarm-manager only; delete any app-issue-tracker test doubles.
5. Document the resulting migration pattern (mapping table: AIT endpoint → swarm-manager endpoint, AIT type → swarm-manager type) in a short note under app-monitor or swarm-manager docs — this becomes the template for the sweep across other scenarios.

## Acceptance
- `rg -n 'app-issue-tracker|appIssueTracker|app_issue_tracker' scenarios/app-monitor` returns zero matches outside removal-history docs.
- App-monitor service.json no longer depends on app-issue-tracker.
- All app-monitor tests pass without app-issue-tracker running.
- Migration mapping doc exists and is referenced by the sweep item below.

item.name: cross-scenario-issue-tracker-cutover-sweep
item.title: Hard-Cutover All Remaining Scenarios Off App-Issue-Tracker to Swarm-Manager
item.description:
Apply the app-monitor cutover pattern to every other scenario that still integrates with app-issue-tracker. Hard cutover only — no compat shims, no fallbacks, no dead code.

## Identified Consumers (from `rg 'app-issue-tracker' scenarios/`)

- **scenario-auditor** — substantial integration: `api/handlers_issue_tracker.go`, `api/agent_manager.go`, `api/protected_scenarios_store.go`, `api/rules/config/setup_steps.go`, `api/rules/structure/test_coverage.go`, UI `ReportIssueDialog.tsx`, `RulesManager.tsx`, `ManageProtectedScenariosDialog.tsx`.
- **deployment-manager** — `ui/src/pages/Deployments.tsx`, `ui/src/components/GuidedFlow.tsx`, plus docs/scenarios refs.
- **prd-control-tower** — `api/issues.go`.
- **landing-manager** — `api/handlers/customize.go`, `api/errors/errors.go`, `ui/src/components/AgentCustomizationForm.tsx`.
- **secrets-manager** — `ui/src/sections/TierReadiness.tsx`.
- **agent-inbox** — `api/domain/types.go`.
- **scenario-dependency-analyzer** — `api/internal/app/analysis_test.go` (test-only).
- **vrooli-orchestrator** — `initialization/postgres/seed.sql`.
- **swarm-manager itself** — `requirements/18-app-issue-tracker-integration/module.json` (rewrite or retire).
- **prompt-manager team docs / agent SOULs** referencing AIT (oss-advertiser) — text-only updates.

Re-run the inventory at start; treat the list above as a hint, not authoritative.

## Per-Scenario Procedure (apply uniformly)
1. Map each AIT call to its swarm-manager equivalent using the doc produced by `app-monitor-issue-tracker-cutover-verify`.
2. Replace, don't wrap. Delete the AIT client/types/handlers; add swarm-manager calls in their place.
3. Update service.json depends_on, env wiring, and any deployment manifests.
4. Update or delete tests; do not keep AIT mocks 'just in case'.
5. Sweep docs and CLAUDE.md / memory references in the same scenario.
6. Confirm `rg 'app-issue-tracker'` for that scenario returns zero non-removal-history hits.

## Out of Scope
- The app-issue-tracker scenario directory itself (handled by the deprecation chore).
- App-monitor (handled by the verify item).

## Acceptance
- Repo-wide `rg -n 'app-issue-tracker|appIssueTracker|app_issue_tracker' scenarios/ | grep -v 'scenarios/app-issue-tracker/'` returns zero non-historical matches.
- All affected scenarios build and pass their own tests with app-issue-tracker NOT running.

mutations.rationale: Brings the deprecation chore in line with the user's hard-cutover requirement and makes the cross-scenario sweep an explicit precondition rather than a one-line afterthought about app-monitor.

patch.description:
Archive the app-issue-tracker scenario after swarm-manager has achieved feature parity AND every consuming scenario has been hard-cutover off it.

## Context

App-issue-tracker was created to track and spawn coding agents to fix issues discovered in other scenarios. Swarm-manager has evolved into a strictly more capable system covering ideas, research, chores, and execution tasks with a richer workshop model, initiative grouping, and graph visualization.

## Pre-Deprecation Checklist

1. **Provenance tracking** (via agent identity standard): swarm-manager tracks who/what created each backlog item with verified identity.
2. **Concurrency / rate limiting** (via concurrency guardrails): swarm-manager has configurable concurrency limits, queue depth, and circuit breaker.
3. **Search and discovery** (via sidebar search): swarm-manager has search, filtering, and tabbed navigation.
4. **One-shot investigation flow**: swarm-manager's queue → execute flow with workshop-optional fast paths covers AIT's investigate endpoint.
5. **All consumers cut over**: app-monitor verified hard-cutover, and every other scenario swept (see `execute/app-monitor-issue-tracker-cutover-verify` and `execute/cross-scenario-issue-tracker-cutover-sweep`). Hard cutover only — no compat shims, no fallbacks, no dead code anywhere in the repo.

## Deliverables

1. **Extract reusable patterns** before removal: automation processor concept (background loop auto-picking open items) → design note for swarm-manager auto-processing; Tool Discovery Protocol v1.0 → API contract note; export format templates (CSV/markdown) → swarm-manager multi-format export note.
2. **Archive the scenario** using the established archive pattern (similar to archive-and-remove-legacy-vrooli-bridge).
3. **Repo-wide sweep**: confirm `rg 'app-issue-tracker'` is empty outside `scenarios/app-issue-tracker/` and removal-history docs. Update CLAUDE.md, memory files, prompt-manager team docs (oss-advertiser SOUL etc.), and `swarm-manager/requirements/18-app-issue-tracker-integration/module.json`.
4. **Verify nothing references AIT at runtime** — service.json depends_on across all scenarios, env wiring, deployment manifests, postgres seed (`vrooli-orchestrator/initialization/postgres/seed.sql`).

mutations.rationale: Deprecation cannot land until app-monitor's cutover is verified clean.
